clue.text: Theologian no go at operatic work

indicators.note: 'no' tells us to do without the short word that follows it in the fodder
the remaining letters are set to work, i.e. busy being rearranged; the signal is weak, as old Gordius clues often were

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A theologian is barred from attending an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip GO from THEOLOGIAN and shuffle the eight letters left. Iolanthe is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe is the title of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, so it is an example of the stage genre.

clue.text: Pander to a sanctimonious politician

blocks.note: pi is informal British for pious or sanctimonious
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone panders to a self-righteous politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pander to' reads as the verb phrase, but Pander alone is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pander is a procurer who arranges sexual liaisons for others, the same trade as a pimp.

clue.text: Fool gets involved in gamble over a dog

indicators.note: something involved in another thing is caught up inside it

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
a bet is a gamble

explanation.surface: An idiot gets mixed up in betting on a dog race.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound breed, so it is one kind of domestic canine.

clue.text: Soldiers lack faith in defence

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to doubt is to lack faith

explanation.surface: Troops losing faith in their defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a fortified outwork or stronghold, a military structure built for protection.

clue.text: End of the line for the House of Hanover

definitions.text: End of the line for the House of Hanover

blocks.note: surface reading: a railway terminus, the last stop
setter's reading: the last monarch of that royal dynasty

explanation.surface: A dynasty reaches the end of its line.
explanation.walkthrough: It works both ways: Victoria is a London railway terminus, and Queen Victoria was the last British monarch of the House of Hanover.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria ended the Hanoverian line, since her son Edward VII took his father's house name.

clue.text: Where to get a cheap jumper?

definitions.text: Where to get a cheap jumper?

blocks.clueFragment: Where to get a cheap jumper?
blocks.note: surface reading: a jumper is a British word for a sweater, bought cheaply at a bargain stall
setter's reading: an insect that jumps, sold at a market named after it

explanation.surface: Asking where to buy an inexpensive sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is a sweater in Britain, which is where the surface points; the jumping insect gives the market its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A street market of cheap secondhand goods, where a bargain pullover could be found, is named after the jumping insect.

clue.text: Soldier makes love with a girl in a leisurely way

blocks.note: a girl's name
an American private soldier
love is zero, as in tennis

explanation.surface: A soldier romances a girl at a slow pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read in the reverse of the clue's order: the girl comes first, then the soldier and love.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is a musical tempo marking meaning slowly, at an easy unhurried pace.

clue.text: Hog the motorway? Give over!

indicators.note: one word laid over another covers it, so it wraps around

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway, written with I for 1
to donate is to give

explanation.surface: An irritated driver tells a road hog to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give over!' is British slang for 'stop it', but here it means put DONATE over the motorway. The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To hog is to take control of and monopolise something, which matches holding sway over it.

clue.text: Guided by instinct, did nothing

blocks.note: the id is Freud's term for the instinctive part of the mind
guided means led

explanation.surface: Someone acting on instinct and doing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says LED is guided by ID, so ID stands beside it, first.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to be inactive and lazy, passing time without working or achieving anything.

clue.text: Find fault with vehicle parking

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Complaining about where a car is parked.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain pettily and continually, criticising small things.

clue.text: Rang from no great  distance

blocks.note: surface reading: telephoned someone
setter's reading: the word for a scope of reach, cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned from nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, makes the clue word. Clip the end off the five-letter word for reach and you have the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-range describes something operating or fired over a small distance, close at hand.

clue.text: Narrow Southern  characteristic

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a trait is a characteristic

explanation.surface: Describing a narrow trait typical of the South.
explanation.definitionFit: Strait is an old adjective for tight or confined, as in strait gate and straitjacket.

clue.text: A drug he's no right to carry?

definitions.text: A drug he's no right to carry?

indicators.note: 'no right' asks for the carry word without its abbreviation for right

blocks.note: taken as written
pot is slang for cannabis
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.surface: Questioning whether someone is entitled to carry drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the answer: an old-style chemist handled drugs that others had no right to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: An apothecary was a historical pharmacist who prepared and sold medicines, so was licensed to hold drugs.

clue.text: In grave recession one's after a little work to bear fruit

indicators.note: 'after' places the single letter for one behind the small unit of work
a recession is a going back, so the burial place is written backwards
'In' puts what follows inside the turned-round burial place

blocks.note: the erg is a small unit of work in physics
a means one
a tomb is a grave

explanation.surface: A recession buries someone's work so it can't bear fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The erg is the physics unit of work, small enough to be 'a little work'; 'grave' wants to be an adjective with recession but is the burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot is a citrus fruit grown in Italy, whose rind oil flavours Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: It's difficult to keep order when she's about

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside
'about' as in about-turn means the result faces the other way

blocks.note: hard means difficult
the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Keeping discipline is hard when a certain woman is around.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD holds OBE to make HOBEARD, and turning that about gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Deborah is a woman's name, and crosswords often use 'she' to stand for any female first name.

clue.text: Dog needs a top class leader for training

indicators.note: something put in for training is drilled and reshaped

blocks.note: A1 means top class, written with I for 1
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog needs a first-rate pack leader to train it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire, so it is a kind of canine.

clue.text: What journalist witnessed is destined for cutting

definitions.note: describes the noun answer as a thing meant for cutting

blocks.note: a hack is a journalist
saw means witnessed

explanation.surface: A reporter's eyewitness copy is bound to be edited down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' looks like editing a reporter's story, but it is sawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed handsaw made for sawing through metal, so it exists to cut.

clue.text: Jack you may forgive

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: one who may forgive

blocks.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB is an able-bodied seaman
you, the reader, are the solver of this puzzle

explanation.surface: You may forgive Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you' is the person doing the crossword, the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolver is a person, such as a priest, who grants pardon or remission of sins.

clue.text: Turkish test included in Western alliance set-up

indicators.note: something included in another sits inside it
in a down clue, set up means raised so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation
the MOT is Britain's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles

explanation.surface: A Turkish test sits within the Western alliance structure.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first, and only then is the whole thing turned upward, as befits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottoman describes the Turkish empire and its people, so it serves as an older term for Turkish.

clue.text: Task covered by worker, a loner

indicators.note: a thing covered by another is enclosed within it

blocks.note: a chore is a task
the worker ant

explanation.surface: A task done by a solitary worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchoret, or anchorite, is a religious recluse who lives in seclusion away from society.

clue.text: Some nasty turn on the briny?

definitions.text: Some nasty turn on the briny?

indicators.note: 'Some' asks for only part of the next word, so most of its letters are dropped

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut down to its opening letters
a U-turn, a turn shaped like the letter
the briny is a jocular name for the sea

explanation.surface: Something nasty happening out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a 'turn' is a bout of feeling ill, and seasickness is a nasty one on the briny.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is the queasy feeling of being about to vomit, typical of seasickness on a rough voyage.

clue.text: Chemical can be made up at shop,  ...

indicators.note: something made up is put together afresh, so the letters are recombined

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist's shop making up a preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next across clue's remedy, but each solves alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound, such as potassium carbonate, used in fertiliser and soap.

clue.text: Soft steel being flexible, it needs mortar

indicators.note: a flexible thing bends out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical term for soft
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flexible steel used in building needs mortar too.
explanation.walkthrough: Mortar suggests bricklaying, but here it is the bowl a pestle grinds in.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped grinding tool used with a mortar bowl; the two always go as a pair.

clue.text: ...  remedy for when the wife collapses?

blocks.note: my old Dutch is Cockney slang for one's wife, from duchess
drops means collapses

explanation.surface: A medicine to give when one's wife faints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My old Dutch' is London Cockney for the wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch drops were an old patent medicine, a preparation of turpentine and oils taken as a cure-all.

clue.text: The key to higher  education?

blocks.note: first meaning: a brand of lock and its flat key
second meaning: a leading American university

explanation.surface: The secret of getting into university.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is both a well-known lock maker whose name is used for its keys, and an Ivy League university in Connecticut.

clue.text: But there are more than three flat feet here

definitions.text: But there are more than three flat feet here

blocks.note: surface reading: a length of three feet laid flat, a measure of distance
setter's reading: flatfoot is slang for a police officer, many of whom work at Scotland's famous headquarters

explanation.surface: A puzzle about measuring length in feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Three feet make the unit, but 'flat feet' are police officers, and Scotland Yard is London's police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a measure of three feet and the short name for Scotland Yard, the Metropolitan Police headquarters.

clue.text: Loner resolved to join

indicators.note: resolved can mean broken down and re-formed, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A solitary person decides to become a member.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up and register as a member of a course or organisation.

clue.text: 100% green product may cause unhealthy reaction

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: something that may cause one

indicators.note: a product is something manufactured, so these letters are processed into a new form

blocks.note: 100% is all of it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Warning that a wholly green product can trigger a bad reaction.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergen is a substance, such as pollen, that triggers an allergic immune response in sensitive people.
